nging action needs confirm:true plus a human approval seam, with a digest-verified self-update and a
settings page. Zero runtime dependencies. | 面向 DSH 的 GitHub 工具：所有写动作都过审批门
# dsh-github-gate
**GitHub tools for DeepSeek Harness where a write cannot happen by accident.**

9 typed `github_*` tools over the GitHub CLI, 61
actions in all. 29 of them are marked destructive a

nd need
`confirm: true` **and** a human approval seam; the four write methods `github_api` accepts
a

re classified at run time.
The model's flag is intent; it is not consent.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Argv arrays, never a shell.** `gh` is spawned with `shell: false`, so model text
cannot become s

hell syntax — structurally, not by filtering.
- **One credential chain, resolved per call.** DSH cre

dential store → `GH_TOKEN` /
`GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth login` → git credential helper. Rotating a to

ken applies
to the next call.
- **Configuration in the GUI.** Settings → Plugins → GitHub: paste a P

AT, test it
against the API, see which layer is live. The token is never displayed back.
- **A branc

h pill** in the session header: current branch, its pull request, and a
switch menu that fails close

d when the caller cannot be judged.
- **Digest-verified self-update.** `github_update` stages a rele

ase whose sha256 is
checked against the digest GitHub publishes.
Host-side tools plus one small browser half. 0 runtime dependencies. No build step.

> **Requires** DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0` and the
> GitHub CLI (`gh`) on `PATH`. Linux, mac

eepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0` and the
> GitHub CLI (`gh`) on `PATH`. Linux, macOS, and Windows.
**Topics:** `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness` · `dsh` · `cordis-plugin` · `github` · `gh-cli`
## Why this over another GitHub plugin

Tool count is a bad proxy for usefulness — a broader surface with looser gates is
easier to write an
d harder to trust. The trade this project makes is explicit:
| | Other GitHub plugins for DSH | This one |
| Write safety | `confirm: true`, set by the model | `confirm: true` **+** an approval seam the mode

l cannot set |
| Raw REST | unrestricted escape hatch | path must be relative, no `..`, write method

s gated at run time |
| Correctness evidence | tests of its own API | 207 tests, 180 behaviour snaps

hots, and **84 argv shapes parsed by a real `gh`** |
| Failure messages | HTTP code passed through |

401 / 403 quota / 403 SSO / 404 / 422 each name the fix |
| Scope | as many tools as possible | 9 t

ools / 61 actions, one to a `gh` subcommand family |
| Self-update | — | staged with a verified sha2
56, install left to the platform |

If you want the largest possible tool surface with no gates, this is not the right
plugin. If you wa

nt the model to be able to *look* at GitHub freely but need a
person in the loop before it *changes*

e able to *look* at GitHub freely but need a
person in the loop before it *changes* anything, it is.
## Install

Two ways, both through the Harness plugin manager (`plugin_manager` action
`install_bundle`):

1. **From a GitHub release** — download `dsh-github-gate-<version>.tgz` from
Releases and point `ins

tall_bundle` at the unpacked package
directory, or at a local path holding it.
2. **From a packed ta
rball of your own checkout**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
then install `../packages/dsh-github-gate-<version>.tgz`.

**Install from a packed tarball, not from the source directory.** This is not a
style preference. In

stalling a `link:` to a workspace directory produces a
junction, and the launcher's runtime resoluti

on does not reach bare
[该节后续省略]
### Why `peerDependencies` are declared

The plugin imports `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (its Config schema) and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (`def

ineTool`). The runtime resolution decides what to
supply from the plugin's own manifest — `profileDe

pendencyNames` reads
`dependencies` and `peerDependencies` — so a bare import that is **not**
declar

ed cannot resolve, and the plugin dies at import. The declared ranges
admit the running dsh version,

which is what keeps
`evaluatePluginCompatibility` from demanding a version exemption.
## What it provides
| Tool | Covers |
| `github_auth` | Credential chain status, **end-to-end connectivity probe**, Device Flow login, PAT

login, logout |
| `github_repo` | View, list, branches, clone, create, edit, rename, archive, delet

e |
| `github_pr` | List, view, diff, checks, status, create, comment, review, ready, checkout, merg

e, close, reopen, edit |
| `github_issue` | List, view, create, comment, close, reopen, edit, develo

p |
| `github_release` | List, view, create, edit, upload, download, delete |
| `github_actions` | R

un list/view/log/watch/rerun/cancel/delete, workflow list/view/dispatch |
| `github_search` | Reposi

tories, issues, pull requests, code, commits |
| `github_api` | Guarded raw REST for everything else

(registered when `allowRawApi: true`) |
| `github_update` | Check for a newer release of this plugi
n, and stage its verified tarball |
## Known limitations

- **Device Flow has not completed a real authorization round trip.** The polling
state machine is fu

lly covered against an injected fetch; the real github.com
exchange needs your own OAuth App and a b

rowser.
- **No write action has been executed.** All verification is read-only; no real
resource was

created, merged, or deleted.
- **Only `github_auth` action `token` prints a token.** It exists to p

ipe a token
into another tool, so its `stdout` is the secret; the plugin never puts one in
argv, in

a log line, or in a card. Treat that output as a secret. Everything else
reports *which layer* suppl

ied the credential and never the value. Tool cards go
through the generic `presentCall`/`presentResu

lt` path with a real `kind`
(read / search).
- **Source edits do not take effect automatically**: th

e installed artifact is a
tarball snapshot.
- **PTC mode is untested.** `defineTool` makes `await to

ols.<name>(args)` work, but
this plugin has not been driven under the PTC preset.

Designs that were evaluated and deliberately not implemented — structured review
evidence routing, i

dempotent PR creation, diff budgets, flow state — are recorded
in docs/DESIGN.md §8 so the ideas are

not lost with the source
repositories.
